description: Case no. 26-009 MA – 450 Charles Street Applicant: 329 Development LLC The applicant is requesting to combine master and preliminary plan approval to construct a building that will serve as a contractor's storage yard in the M-1 zone. The applicant is requesting waivers from submission of state approvals and a signage plan at the preliminary plan stage – for vote (AP 76 Lot 529, Charles) Mr. Manjrekar introduced the item. Attorney Joseph Carnevale presented the item with engineers David Bray and Kevin Harrop. He explained the project's design and said commercial projects had previously been approved for the site and was suited for development. DRC Application No. 19.03: 2 Kennedy Plaza (Alex and Ani City Center) Proposal by the City of Providence to alter the existing roof of the City Center Building by removing the center viewing porch and roof. Bonnie Nickerson, Planning Director, and Glen Fontecchio, architect, appeared to present the project. A powerpoint presentation as made. Ms. Nickerson explained that the building is a gateway, but also a visual barrier into the rink and beyond to Union Station. She presented the Greater Kennedy Plaza Vision Plan, noting that the initial plan was to remove the building in its entirety; however, the Parks Department wants to keep the existing businesses in the building. The plan now calls for the partial removal of the existing roof over the three center bays and its support columns. She explained that the reason for the removal of the center portion is due to the new Downtown Transit Circulator shelter which is to be located in the East Approach roadway. The roadway, which now currently provides vehicular and truck access into the rink (for events), is to be permanently closed. If assisted real property is not used to meet a national objective, the subrecipient must reimburse the local CDBG account an amount equal to the prorated share of the current fair market value of the property. In this case, the proposed redevelopment plan for the property remains CDBG-eligible under §570.203(b), and will meet a separate national objective, §570.208(a)(4), through the creation of jobs to be made available to low/moderate income area residents. DISCUSSION REGARDING A NOTICE OF CHANGE IN USE PURSUANT TO 24 CFR 570.505 – BOMES THEATER REDEVELOPMENT Pursuant to 24 CFR 570.505 and 570.503(b)(7), the Bomes Theater property at 1017 Broad Street—originally acquired by the Providence Redevelopment Agency with federal CDBG funds for the purposes of historic preservation and spot blight remediation (§570.208(b)(2))—must continue to be used to meet one of the national objectives in 24 CFR 570.208. If assisted real property is not used to meet a national objective, the subrecipient must reimburse the local CDBG account an amount equal to the prorated share of the current fair market value of the property. In this case, the proposed redevelopment plan for the property remains CDBG-eligible under §570.203(b), and will meet a separate national objective, §570.208(a)(4), through the creation of jobs to be made available to low/moderate income area residents. The public is afforded the opportunity to comment on this proposed change in use. ADJOURNMENT
